structural_notes:
WHAT SURVIVES vs WHAT MOVES

All four analyses agree on the frame, and I confirmed it at source: last year's ACTS -> PhreakMe change was not really a frequency change at all. ACTS already used 1700+2200; the author only re-roled them, decomposing a simultaneous pair into an ordered two-symbol alphabet {A,B} and re-encoding value in the degrees of freedom that decomposition created — level (nickel vs dime), order (quarter = A then B), simultaneity ('$' = A+B) — then flattening ACTS' 66/33 ms bursts to a uniform 60/60 grid. The grammar was the invention. You do not re-invent a grammar two years running. So "a change similar to last year's" means the same six-symbol grammar with the pair relocated.

Hold these constant while sweeping: 60 ms tone / 60 ms silence, 'return' at 15 ms gaps, 2 ms raised-cosine fades, 8 kHz/16-bit/mono; nickel and dime the same tone separated only by level; quarter an ordered sequence, not a burst count; collect = 3x A, return = 6x A; '$' = A+B simultaneous. Also keep the combined-level convention — per-component amplitude is 10^(L/20)/k (tone_engine.py:129-160), so a single-tone nickel at -6 dBFS is genuinely 6 dB down while each leg of a two-tone '$' at -3 dBFS is about -9 dBFS. Do not "normalise" this; amplitude is semantic, and rescaling silently converts a nickel into a dime.

THE SEARCH SPACE IS 42, AND WHY

detect_mf_samples (tone_engine.py:412) runs a Goertzel over exactly _MF_ALL_FREQS = [700, 900, 1100, 1300, 1500, 1700, 2200]. A carrier outside that list is invisible to the author's own decoder, so the simultaneous '$' primitive could not decode at all. Nyquist at FS=8000 and the 300-3400 passband independently forbid anything higher. 7 x 6 = 42 ordered pairs — one evening of calls, and exactly what softblue/redbox.py candidates() enumerates. Note 2600 is deliberately absent, so no 2600-based coin scheme is detectable.

DISAGREEMENT 1 — THE BIG ONE: IS A BOUND PAIR DISQUALIFIED?

Three analyses put 1500+2200 first. The fourth EXCLUDES it entirely, on the grounds that _MF_DECODE (keyed by frozenset, tone_engine.py:313-322) already binds it as coin ST, so a 1500+2200 '$' would decode as a register symbol. That analysis instead derives the five free pairs — (700,2200), (900,1700), (900,2200), (1100,2200), (1300,2200) — kills three on physics, and lands on 900+2200. I verified the census: it is exactly right, and 1500 is indeed the one frequency with NO free partner (all six are bound by digits 7/8/9/0, Bell ST and coin ST).

I resolved this in favour of 1500+2200 (rank 2) with 900+2200 close behind (rank 4), because the precedent falsifies the premise: last year's own '$' is 1700+2200, which IS coin KP — a deliberate collision. The author wrote it down as a known wart in his own spec (Tone Engine.md:170: "'$' frequencies == coin KP frequencies ... the detector side must disambiguate"). Collision is therefore this author's demonstrated practice, not a disqualifier. The dissent still has real force in one direction though: if the author decided to FIX that wart this year, he must pick a free pair — and that is precisely the argument for ranks 4 and 7. Read a null result on ranks 2/3/5 as evidence for the collision-free family and jump to 4 and 7.

DISAGREEMENT 2 — HARMONIC FOLDING KILLS TWO POPULAR PICKS

2 x 1100 = 2200 exactly (the marker) and 2 x 1300 = 2600 exactly (detect_2600_samples). One analysis measured the false-trip thresholds with the server's own Goertzel: at a -3 dBFS fundamental, either victim detector (threshold -35 dBFS) trips once 2nd-harmonic distortion is worse than -32 dBc; at -6 dBFS, -29 dBc. Both are trivially exceeded by acoustic coupling. The other three analyses ranked 1100+2200 and 1300+2200 in their top 7 on motive alone. I split the difference: 1300+2200 stays at 7 (a clean synthesised sine has negligible H2, and the author plausibly never ran the check), 1100+2200 drops to 13 (the octave case is far worse — B is literally A's harmonic, so a nickel can present as a '$').

DISAGREEMENT 3 — THE BRIEF'S _MF_BELL TABLE IS WRONG

Three analyses caught this and I confirmed it at tone_engine.py:41-50. The real table has KP=(1100,1700), ST=(1500,1700), KP2=(1300,1700), ST3=(700,1700). There is NO ST2 entry and NO 900+1700 symbol anywhere. This is load-bearing: under the brief's table the free intra-Bell pair would have been 700+1700; under the real file it is 900+1700, which is what makes 900 the alphabet's unique spare and underwrites rank 4. Separately, softblue/engine.py MF_SPECIAL disagrees with the server the same way — softblue's "ST3" (1300+1700) decodes server-side as KP2, softblue's "ST2" (900+1700) is not in _MF_DECODE at all so detect_mf_samples returns None, and the server's real ST3 (700+1700) is unreachable from softblue. Irrelevant to coins, but it will bite on a blue-box challenge.

THE THREE MOVES THIS RANKED LIST STRUCTURALLY CANNOT EXPRESS

Three of the four analyses independently flagged that a (freq_a, freq_b) pair cannot represent the change they consider most likely on the merits. RedboxScheme pins nickel, dime, collect and return all to freq_a and uses freq_b only for the quarter's second symbol and the dollar's partner. Outside that shape:

(A) THREE-SYMBOL ALPHABET, LEVEL ENCODING RETIRED — e.g. nickel=900, dime=1700, quarter=1700->2200. This is the strongest non-pair hypothesis and arguably the strongest hypothesis overall. Level-only encoding is the one part of last year's scheme the author's OWN RECEIVER CANNOT READ: detect_coin_samples (tone_engine.py:453-463) returns a bare (has_1700, has_2200) tuple, and its only consumer, _check_coin_tones in agi/ctf_processor.agi:1805-1835, just logs presence. Nothing anywhere on the receive path measures amplitude, so the server literally cannot tell a nickel from a dime today. Giving each denomination its own frequency fixes that AND satisfies "the frequencies changed". If the coin-control triple is used, the closed canonical set is the green box {700, 1100, 1700} (collect / return / ringback). SIGNATURE: quarter accepted but nickel and dime both rejected, or both credited as the same value. If you see that, stop sweeping pairs and probe bare single tones at each of the seven frequencies.
(B) BURST COUNT RESTORED on top of the new pair (nickel=1xA, dime=2xA) — a partial return to ACTS.
(C) DURATION AS THE VALUE ENCODER (nickel=A@60ms, dime=A@120ms, same tone and level).

Repo extension if you want to cover these: give RedboxScheme per-symbol overrides (freq_nickel, freq_dime, freq_quarter_1, freq_quarter_2) defaulting to A/A/A/B. The engine already supports it — Config.coin_spec and ToneEngine._build_phreakme_coin take an arbitrary per-symbol segment list, so only the search-space generator needs changing.

HOW TO SPEND THE CALL MINUTES

0. BEFORE SWEEPING AT ALL: try blind recovery. sweep.py scan_segments() recovers frequency from the spectrum, level from the envelope and duration from run length with no priors, and segments_to_coin_spec() feeds it straight into a --coin-spec file. Two routes to a capture: (i) the deep dive (:264-265) says the organisers hand out complimentary tone generation devices at the payphone area — record one; (ii) provoke the challenge into emitting its own coin-collect or coin-return signal, which are the loudest and most distinctive patterns in the scheme (3 pulses and 6 pulses). One clean capture collapses this entire 18-candidate list to a single answer and beats every prediction here.
1. Dial rank 1 (control) first — establishes the baseline Fingerprint and tells you whether anything moved at all.
2. Then 2, 3, 4, 5. That covers the top prediction, the reversal, the collision-free pick and the best correction in four calls.
3. PROBE WITH THE QUARTER, NOT THE NICKEL. The quarter is the only symbol that exercises A, B and their ORDER in one burst, and it carries no level semantics — so a miss is unambiguously a frequency miss. Only once a quarter is accepted should you sweep the nickel/dime split. This separates the frequency dimension from the level dimension instead of confounding them. Where the challenge lets you choose a denomination for the actual solve, prefer the quarter or '$' — never stake a solve on a 3 dB difference across an acoustic path.
4. Run rank 17 (66 ms timing null) early despite its rank — it is cheap and eliminates a whole branch.

DIAGNOSTIC READINGS
- Control still credited, nothing else changes -> nothing moved; go to rank 18 (level polarity) and rank 17 (timing).
- Coin accepted but AMOUNT wrong -> level semantics moved, not frequencies; rank 18, then rank 10.
- Nickel/dime credited but quarter not -> only freq_b moved: "kept the workhorse, moved the marker"; ranks 9 and 6.
- Nothing credited at all -> the workhorse moved; ranks 2, 4, 5, 7 (the keep-the-2200-guard family).
- Quarter accepted, nickel and dime both rejected or both credited identically -> the three-symbol hypothesis (A above); stop sweeping pairs.
- Ranks 3 and 5 fail while 2200-as-marker candidates partially respond -> suspect the FXO path, not the scheme (Tone Engine.md:171 admits 2200 Hz response through the HT813 is unverified).

TWO FIXES NEEDED IN softblue BEFORE THE SWEEP RUNS

1. sweep.py:118 PHREAKME_FREQ_POOL = (1700.0, 2200.0, 1500.0, 1300.0) cannot express ranks 4, 11, 12, 14 or 16. Widen it to the full MF_ALPHABET (700, 900, 1100, 1300, 1500, 1700, 2200). candidates_phreakme(two_tone=True) then yields 42 ordered pairs per duration. One analysis argued for pruning to (900, 2200, 1700, 700) instead, on the grounds that 1500 has no free partner and 1300 folds onto 2600 — I disagree with pruning, because that argument rests on the collision premise falsified in Disagreement 1 above, and it would delete this list's top prediction.
2. redbox.py:67-69 is_control compares only (freq_a, freq_b) and duration, so rank 18 (the level inversion) is misidentified as the control and hijacks the sweep's baseline. Either drive rank 18 by hand, or extend is_control to also require nickel_dbfs == -6.0 and dime_dbfs == -3.0. Note also that load_ranked() preserves file order and does not re-sort, which is why the control must lead the ranked file — matching the fixture at tests/test_redbox.py:118-128.

RESIDUAL RISK THAT NO PAIR SWEEP CAN COVER

detect_coin_samples hard-codes 1700.0 and 2200.0. ANY frequency move forces the author into that function. Once he is editing detector code, nothing stops him extending _MF_ALL_FREQS itself and putting the coin pair outside the R1 set — 2400 Hz (CCITT #5 line signalling, documented in dc34-phreakme/ccitt-c5-c4-signaling.md but never yet used for coins) is the single most likely out-of-alphabet addition. One analysis proposed 2400->2600 outright; I excluded it per the constraint that every candidate must be measurable by the server's detector, and note that 2600 would additionally fire detect_2600_samples on every deposit. I rate the out-of-alphabet scenario unlikely — the whole design leans on 2200 being "the coin-identification guard" precisely because it is the one frequency with real payphone meaning — but if all 18 candidates miss, that is the next hypothesis, and blind recovery (step 0) is the only reliable answer to it.

Ranked 4 rather than 1 because it requires the author to have run the collision analysis, and last year he demonstrably did NOT — he shipped '$'=coin KP as a known collision.

Both operations at once: relocate to the coin ST pair AND invert the order, so 2200 carries value and 1500 is the marker. Breaks every symbol including '$'. Same two-constant edit cost as rank 2, and it is the most likely correction if rank 2 produces a partial or ambiguous reaction — dial it immediately after rank 2 rather than in strict rank order. Ranked below rank 2 because it inverts the author's stated doctrine that 2200 identifies the call as a coin call rather than carrying the value.

Retaining 1700 also means half-hardcoded tools partially work, diluting the break.

The 'fix the flagged ambiguity' branch, and the subject of a live disagreement (see structural_notes). Case for: frozenset{1300,2200} is NOT a key in _MF_DECODE, so a 1300+2200 '$' can never be misread as KP or ST — it retires the exact open item the author wrote into his own spec (Tone Engine.md:170). 1300 is already discoverable from published material as KP2's low member (1300+1700), and 900 Hz of separation keeps the Goertzel bins clean. Case against: 2 x 1300 = 2600 EXACTLY, landing on detect_2600_samples (threshold -35 dBFS) on a trunk whose whole premise is in-band 2600 seizure. Measured arithmetic: with the fundamental at -3 dBFS, the 2600 detector false-trips as soon as 2nd-harmonic distortion is worse than -32 dBc — trivially exceeded by acoustic coupling. 1300 also folds H5 onto 1500 Hz. Three analyses rank it mid, one rules it out on that harmonic. I keep it at 7 because a clean synthesised sine has negligible H2 and the author may simply not have run the check.

Two independent routes land here. (a) The 'de-coin it' move: split standard Bell ST (1500+1700, _MF_BELL['ST']) into the alphabet, mirroring last year's operation applied to a Bell pair instead of a coin pair. (b) The mechanical ladder shift: MF frequencies form a 200 Hz ladder, and stepping last year's {1700,2200} down one rung each gives 1700->1500 and 2200->1700, landing exactly on a real canonical tone. Ladder shifts appeal to authors because they are trivially reproducible year over year. THIRD and most interesting route: this is the pair the organisers' own lab README (03-redboxing/README.md:20-24) mislabels as 'Standard Bell ACTS — 1700+1500 Hz', which is factually wrong (real ACTS is 1700+2200, as deep_dive:1179 correctly states). If the author works from his own erroneous secondary source when composing 'the historical baseline we are moving back toward', this pair becomes far likelier than its intrinsic merit. Weakness: 2200 vanishes, and '$' becomes Bell ST.

The partial-break / high-diagnostic branch: keep 1700 as the workhorse, demote the marker from 2200 to 1500. Nickel, dime, collect and return all keep working with last year's red box; only the quarter and '$' change. An author who wanted the easy coins to stay solved and only the quarter to become the puzzle would do exactly this. It is a weak fit for 'they changed the frequencies' — which is why it sits at 9 — but its diagnostic value is the highest in the list: if last year's nickel is still credited and only the quarter fails, freq_a did not move at all and the sweep collapses from 42 candidates to 6.

Rank 2's pair with the nickel/dime split widened from 3 dB to 6 dB. Level is the ONLY thing separating nickel from dime, and it is the least survivable part of the design: measured at the detector, nickel reads -12.3 dB and dime -9.3 dB, exactly 3.0 dB apart, so any path gain error over 1.5 dB flips one into the other. softblue's own AcousticPath._agc models handset AGC at 4:1, which compresses that 3 dB to about 0.75 dB. An author who watched players fail on nickel-vs-dime at the last event would widen the split while moving the pair. Do not dial this in rank order — dial it immediately after rank 2 if rank 2 gets the quarter accepted but nickel/dime rejected, which is the signature of exactly this.

The mirror-image one-carrier swap: keep 1700 as workhorse, retire 2200, promote 900 to marker. 900+1700 is the ONLY unassigned pair inside the Bell 6-tone group, so it is the only way to build a coin alphabet living entirely in R1 territory. This candidate exists solely because of a correction to the task brief: the brief listed _MF_BELL as containing ST2=(900,1700), but I verified the real file (tone_engine.py:41-50) has NO 900+1700 entry at all — it has KP2=(1300,1700) and ST3=(700,1700). Under the brief's table the free intra-Bell pair would have been 700+1700 and 900 would have had one free partner instead of two. Ranked low: dropping 2200 discards the coin guard every published document leans on, and with both symbols inside the MF digit group a stray coin burst is a component of digits 1/3/5/8 (900) or of KP/ST/KP2/ST3 (1700) — a step backwards in confusability.

Green box / TSPS COIN COLLECT (softblue/engine.py GREEN_BOX). The only pair in the entire canon whose literal meaning is 'take the coin', and the transformation matches last year's exactly in kind: take a canonical simultaneous coin-control pair, split it into an ordered alphabet, keep the simultaneous form as '$'. Supporting observation: the server's existing 'collect' and 'return' primitives (tone_engine.py:112-113) are fakes — just 1700 Hz repeated 3x and 6x, carrying no green-box frequencies at all. Upgrading those to the real TSPS control pairs is a phreak-literate move that also breaks last year's tools. Ranked low because only one analysis raised it, because 700+1100 is MF digit '2' so '$' decodes as a digit, and because the green-box argument really predicts a change to collect/return rather than to nickel/dime/quarter.

DEMOTED ON PHYSICS, not on motive — and this is a flagged disagreement. Motive is good (unassigned in _MF_DECODE, 1100 is Bell KP's low member, keeps the 2200 guard) and two analyses rank it 4th-5th. But 2 x 1100 = 2200 EXACTLY: symbol B is symbol A's own second harmonic, the only true octave pair in _MF_ALL_FREQS. Any nonlinearity in speaker, handset mic, AGC or mu-law quantisation makes a lone 'A' burst read as 'A+B' — a nickel presenting as a '$' deposit. Quantified against the server's own threshold: with the fundamental at -3 dBFS, detect_coin_samples' 2200 branch false-trips once 2nd-harmonic distortion is worse than -32 dBc; at -6 dBFS, -29 dBc. Both are trivially exceeded acoustically. This codebase is careful about exactly this bug class (see the 150 Hz guard band in tone_engine._self_check:212), so the author would likely have rejected it. Keep in the sweep only as tail coverage.

Unassigned in _MF_DECODE, widest separation in the alphabet (1500 Hz), harmonically tolerable (700's H3=2100 sits 100 Hz off 2200). Disqualified by a subtle DTMF collision I verified in source: _goertzel_power (tone_engine.py:200) computes k = round(n * f_hz / FS), which puts 697 Hz and 700 Hz in the IDENTICAL bin at every plausible coin duration — at 60 ms, n=480, both give k=42; likewise k=23 at 33 ms, k=46 at 66 ms, k=56 at 80 ms, k=70 at 100 ms. A 700 Hz coin burst therefore presents as a full-scale DTMF row-1 to detect_dtmf_samples, and any concurrent column energy synthesises a spurious 1/2/3/A. Kept in the grid because the author may simply not have read the rounding, but it is a design error and so unlikely to be the intended answer.

KP2 (1300+1700) split into the alphabet — the third and last named 1700-pair in _MF_BELL after KP and ST, completing the 'split a named pair from the author's own table' family. Same '$'-collides-with-a-register-symbol objection as ranks 6 and 8, and KP2 is the least prominent of the three in the published docs. Tail coverage.

Green box RINGBACK (GREEN_BOX['b']=(700,1700)), simultaneously CCITT #5 Code 11 'bring in the inward operator', and the symbol whopper already carries as ST3 (tone_engine.py:49 — note the brief did not list this pair, but the real file has it). Completes the green-box triple {700,1100,1700}. Ranked here because ringback is the least coin-valued of the three green-box meanings; if probing suggests the scheme moved into the green-box family at all, test all three pairs (12, 6, 16) together.

TIMING-AXIS NULL TEST. Frequencies unchanged; segment length restored to the ACTS-canonical 66 ms from the uniform 60 ms imposed last year. Part of last year's departure from ACTS was collapsing 66/33 ms bursts to a flat 60/60 grid, so 'a similar change' could mean reverting toward heritage timing. Contestants would report this as 'they changed the frequencies' because a 60 ms probe against a 66 ms detector window fails in exactly the same silent way a wrong frequency does. Their stated tolerance is +/-10 ms (Tone Engine.md 4.3), so 60 and 66 are only separable if they also tightened the detector — which makes this cheap to rule out and worth doing early despite the rank. Also probe the quarter at 33 ms. A frequency sweep structurally cannot see this axis.

LEVEL-AXIS TEST — quieter is now the dime, louder the nickel. Last year's signature innovation was making amplitude carry value; inverting the polarity is a one-character edit that silently breaks every red box built on the 'louder = more money' comment at tone_engine.py:101, while staying trivially discoverable from a recording. Completely invisible to any frequency sweep. Dial this if rank 1 still gets a coin-accepted reaction but the credited AMOUNT is wrong. IMPLEMENTATION WARNING: this entry shares the control's (freq_a, freq_b, duration), so RedboxScheme.is_control (softblue/redbox.py:67-69) returns True for it — the sweep will mistake it for the baseline. Drive it by hand, or extend is_control to compare levels too (see structural_notes).
